description: LongMemEval-style benchmark fixture: expanded baseline with distractor facts, overlapping titles, paraphrased bodies, and multi-domain coverage. 45 facts, 30 questions across 6 sessions. Evaluates FTS5 retrieval quality under controlled lexical noise.

facts.title: JWT signing uses RS256 with 2048-bit RSA
facts.body: All JWT tokens are signed using RS256 with a 2048-bit RSA key pair. The public key is available at /.well-known/jwks.json. Key rotation happens every 90 days via the key_rotation cron job.

facts.title: Alternative JWT signing with ES256 considered
facts.body: ES256 with P-256 curve was evaluated as a faster alternative to RS256. Benchmarks showed 40% faster signing but verification was slower. Decision was to stick with RS256 for ecosystem compatibility.

facts.title: Session TTL configured to 24 hours
facts.body: User sessions expire after 24 hours of inactivity. The TTL is configured via SESSION_TTL_HOURS env var, defaulting to 24. Active sessions are extended on each authenticated request.

facts.title: Login endpoint rate limited to 5/min per IP
facts.body: The login endpoint applies a rate limit of 5 attempts per minute per IP address. Exceeding this triggers a 429 response with a Retry-After header. Failed attempts are counted in Redis with a sliding window.

facts.title: Admin panel rate limited to 10/min
facts.body: The admin panel has a separate rate limit of 10 requests per minute per IP. This is 2x the standard login rate limit to accommodate admin workflows.

facts.title: OAuth login supports Google and GitHub providers
facts.body: The application supports OAuth 2.0 login via Google and GitHub. Provider configuration is stored in the oauth_providers table. Each provider has its own client ID and secret managed via Vault.

facts.title: Refresh tokens use rotation with reuse detection
facts.body: When a refresh token is used, the old token is invalidated and a new refresh token is issued. Reuse detection triggers revocation of all tokens for that user. The rotation window is 30 seconds.

facts.title: User passwords hashed with bcrypt cost factor 12
facts.body: User passwords are hashed using bcrypt with cost factor 12. Legacy accounts with cost 10 are re-hashed on next successful login. The hashing takes approximately 250ms on production hardware.

facts.title: Bcrypt cost factor configurable via env var
facts.body: The bcrypt cost factor can be overridden via BCRYPT_COST env var. Default is 12. Increasing beyond 14 is not recommended as login latency exceeds 500ms.

facts.title: MFA implemented with TOTP 6-digit codes
facts.body: Multi-factor authentication uses TOTP (RFC 6238) with 6-digit codes and a 30-second time step. Backup codes are 8-character alphanumeric strings, one-time use only.

facts.title: Schema migrations managed by golang-migrate v4
facts.body: All schema migrations are managed by golang-migrate v4. Migration files are numbered sequentially and stored in internal/store/migrations/. Each migration has up and down scripts.

facts.title: golang-migrate upgraded to v4.17 for SQLite fixes
facts.body: Upgraded golang-migrate from v4.15 to v4.17 to fix a transaction handling bug in SQLite migrations that caused partial schema states on rollback.

facts.title: SQLite WAL journal mode enabled globally
facts.body: Every SQLite connection opens with PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL. This is enforced in the connection setup in store.go. WAL mode allows concurrent reads during writes.

facts.title: FTS5 index rebuilt during migration 005
facts.body: Migration 005 drops and recreates the FTS5 content table to include the new body column. The rebuild is idempotent and runs in a single transaction.

facts.title: Database connection pool capped at 25 connections
facts.body: The sql.DB connection pool is configured with SetMaxOpenConns(25) and SetMaxIdleConns(5). These values were tuned for the 4-core production instances with moderate query load.

facts.title: Connection pool leak fixed in health check handler
facts.body: The health check endpoint was not closing rows after querying the database, causing a slow connection leak. Fixed by adding defer rows.Close() in the health handler.

facts.title: Database backups use SQLite .backup command daily
facts.body: Automated backups run daily at 02:00 UTC using the SQLite .backup command. Backups are compressed with zstd and stored in S3 with 30-day retention.

facts.title: REST API versioned with /v1/ URL prefix
facts.body: The REST API follows a URL-prefix versioning strategy: all endpoints are prefixed with /v1/. Breaking changes introduce a new /v2/ prefix while /v1/ is deprecated for 6 months. Deprecation is signaled via the Sunset HTTP header.

facts.title: API errors follow RFC 7807 Problem Details format
facts.body: All API errors are returned as application/problem+json with type, title, status, and detail fields. Validation errors include an errors array with per-field messages.

facts.title: Custom error types for auth and rate limiting
facts.body: Authentication errors use type 'about:blank' with status 401. Rate limit errors use a custom type URI and include Retry-After in both header and response body.

facts.title: List endpoints use cursor-based pagination
facts.body: List endpoints use cursor-based pagination with a page_token query parameter. The cursor is an opaque base64-encoded string containing the last item ID and sort key.

facts.title: Cache-Control headers configured on GET responses
facts.body: GET responses include Cache-Control: private, max-age=60 for authenticated endpoints. Public endpoints use max-age=300. ETag headers enable conditional requests.

facts.title: CORS restricted to app.example.com origin
facts.body: The CORS middleware restricts Access-Control-Allow-Origin to https://app.example.com. Preflight OPTIONS requests are cached for 1 hour. Credentials are allowed.

facts.title: Prometheus metrics served on port 9090
facts.body: The application exposes Prometheus metrics on a separate HTTP server listening on port 9090. The /metrics endpoint is not exposed on the main API port to prevent scraping attacks.

facts.title: Internal metrics on port 9091 for health probes
facts.body: A second metrics server on port 9091 exposes internal Go runtime metrics (goroutines, GC, memory) for the health probe system. This port is not exposed externally.

facts.title: Health check endpoint at GET /healthz
facts.body: The /healthz endpoint returns 200 if the database and all upstream dependencies are reachable. It returns 503 otherwise with a JSON body listing each failing check and its latency.

facts.title: Structured logging uses Go slog with JSON output
facts.body: All logging uses Go's slog package with JSON output format. Log level is controlled by LOG_LEVEL env var (debug, info, warn, error). Request IDs are injected via middleware into every log line.

facts.title: Audit log events written at info level to separate file
facts.body: Audit log entries are written at info level to a separate audit.log file using a dedicated slog handler. This ensures audit trail integrity even if debug logging is enabled.

facts.title: Graceful shutdown drains requests with 30s deadline
facts.body: On SIGTERM or SIGINT, the server stops accepting new requests, drains in-flight requests with a 30-second timeout, then closes database connections and flushes logs.

facts.title: SIGKILL handling falls back to immediate exit
facts.body: SIGKILL cannot be trapped, so the application relies on SQLite WAL recovery on next startup. No data loss occurs because all writes are in WAL before committing.

facts.title: Deployments use blue-green strategy with traffic shifting
facts.body: Production deployments use a blue-green strategy. New instances start on alternate ports, pass health checks, then receive traffic via Envoy weight shifting over 60 seconds.

facts.title: Rollback procedure triggers on error rate spike
facts.body: Automatic rollback triggers if the 5xx error rate exceeds 5% for 2 consecutive minutes after deployment. Rollback reverts to the previous Envoy cluster within 15 seconds.

facts.title: CI pipeline runs tests, lint, and benchmarks
facts.body: The CI pipeline runs on every PR: unit tests (go test ./...), lint (golangci-lint), and benchmarks (go test -bench=. -benchtime=100ms ./bench/...). Failures block merge.

facts.title: TLS 1.3 enforced with modern cipher suites
facts.body: All external endpoints require TLS 1.3. Cipher suites are restricted to AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305. Certificate rotation happens automatically via cert-manager every 60 days.

facts.title: API gateway handles auth, rate limiting, and routing
facts.body: Envoy proxy serves as the API gateway, handling JWT validation, IP-based rate limiting, request routing, and TLS termination. Configuration is managed via Kubernetes ConfigMaps.

facts.title: Gateway response caching for read-heavy endpoints
facts.body: Envoy is configured with response caching for GET /v1/config and GET /v1/status endpoints. Cache TTL is 5 minutes. Cache is bypassed when X-Bypass-Cache header is present.

facts.title: Future consideration: database sharding per project
facts.body: As of Q2 2026, database sharding per project is under evaluation. Current single-DB model handles ~500 projects before hitting I/O limits on the 4-core instance.

facts.title: Authentication events recorded in audit log
facts.body: All authentication events (login success, login failure, token refresh, logout) are recorded in the audit_log table with actor ID, timestamp, IP address, and user agent.

facts.title: OAuth provider migration from v1 to v2 endpoints
facts.body: Google OAuth endpoints were migrated from v1 to v2 API in March 2026. The migration required updating redirect URIs and token validation logic. Old endpoints were deprecated.

facts.title: SQLite VACUUM scheduled weekly during low traffic
facts.body: A weekly VACUUM job runs Sunday at 03:00 UTC to reclaim space from deleted records. The operation takes ~45 seconds on the current ~2GB database.

facts.title: API request timeout set to 30 seconds globally
facts.body: All API handlers have a 30-second timeout enforced by the HTTP server. Long-running operations (exports, reports) use async job patterns with polling endpoints.

facts.title: Docker builds use multi-stage with distroless base
facts.body: Production Docker images use multi-stage builds: Go compilation in golang:1.24, runtime in gcr.io/distroless/static. Final image size is 14MB.

facts.title: Prometheus alerts configured for memory and latency
facts.body: AlertManager rules trigger on: heap memory > 80%, p95 latency > 200ms for 5min, error rate > 1%, and database connection pool exhaustion.

facts.title: Secrets managed via HashiCorp Vault with auto-renewal
facts.body: All secrets (API keys, DB passwords, OAuth secrets) are stored in Vault. The application fetches secrets on startup and renews leases every hour. Vault token is injected via Kubernetes.

facts.title: Secrets fallback to env vars for local development
facts.body: When Vault is unavailable (local dev), the application falls back to environment variables. A warning is logged but the application starts normally.
